bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruptions affecting global trade lanes (West Asia hotspot); Volatility in global freight rates impacting GFS pricing; Customer churn in GFS segment; Execution risk in integrating new acquisitions and entering regulated sectors (Defense).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and bullish on FY27; Emphasis on 'spectacular finish' and 'unprecedented growth'; Strategic focus on deepening Fortune 500 relationships and tech-led differentiation; Cautious only on GFS pricing volatility.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Europe business has structurally turned around contributing to margin expansion; Average contract length is highly sticky (4+ years India, 7.5 years Europe); US strategy is deliberately narrow (Auto/Industrial) to mine large accounts rather than broaden verticals too quickly; Integrated Final Mile (IFM) sub-segment has completed corrective actions and is now on a strong profitability path.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- For FY26 the deck reports "Highest ever Revenue of INR 11,003 Cr and Adjusted EBITDA of INR 773 Cr", "INR 243 Cr of Operating Cash Flow" and "Cash and Cash Equivalents of INR 613 Cr, supporting continued investment in growth initiatives".
- Credit rating outlook revised from "Ind AA Stable" to "Ind AA Positive".
- Asset monetisation via InvIT: the P&L note states an "InvIT gain of INR 177.2 Cr. represents share of capital gain on transfer of assets by TVSILP to InvIT", recognised in Q1 FY26 and FY26 and excluded from the deck's Adjusted PBT and Operational PAT definitions.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Century-strong TVS brand heritage and part of the TVS Mobility Group
- End-to-end, integrated 'One TVS SCS' model bundling ISCS and IFM for tailored client solutions
- Asset-light, tech-led operating model with AI and emerging Agentic AI adoption
- Global network combined with strong domestic Indian presence across key trade corridors
- Marquee customer base serving 100 Fortune 500 customers in FY26 (up from 91 in FY25)
- Cost-efficient delivery through the Madurai Centre of Excellence
- Strategic carrier partnerships enabling capacity procurement and service reliability in GFS
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Senior leadership churn at the top — Rapid turnover in key managerial personnel — CEO appointed Jan 22, 2026, Managing Director Ravi Viswanathan resigned effective June 30, 2026, and Vikas Chadha appointed MD effective July 1, 2026 — creates continuity and execution risk at the helm of the business.
- Customer concentration on marquee accounts — Growth is anchored to a relatively small base of large, sophisticated clients (100 Fortune 500 customers serviced, up from 91), and individual strategic contract wins (Global Wind Turbine maker, European retail chain, North America agri-equipment maker); loss or scaling-down of a major account would be material.
- Dependence on continuous new business development — The asset-light, tech-led model relies on winning fresh contracts each year to sustain the topline (FY26 added ~Rs 1,206.74 crores of new-business revenue); a slowdown in wins directly compresses growth.
- Extensive foreign operations and FX / geopolitical exposure — The consolidated group operates through a large web of international subsidiaries across the UK, USA, Germany, Spain, Singapore, Thailand, Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam, Mexico, Indonesia and others, exposing it to currency, cross-border regulatory and geopolitical risk even though standalone exports are Nil.
- Integration and restructuring execution risk — The segment structure was reorganised during FY26 to merge ISCS and IFM (formerly Rico Logistics) into a single unified ISCS model; combining acquired/foreign entities and re-bundling service lines carries integration and execution risk.
- Margin volatility in the asset-light logistics model — Profitability leans on cost-optimisation initiatives and operating leverage from new wins rather than owned assets, leaving margins sensitive to input costs, contract pricing and utilisation swings.
- Cyclicality across served end-markets — Demand is spread across Automotive, FMCG/FMCD, Electronics, E-commerce, Telecom & IT, Oil & Gas, Cement, Retail, Engineering & Capital Goods, Renewable Energy and Healthcare — a downturn in one or more of these cyclical industries flows through to supply-chain volumes.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims to be "India's largest and among the fastest growing integrated supply chain solutions provider" with over 22 years of experience, offering end-to-end solutions through ISCS (sourcing, in-plant operations, aftermarket fulfilment) and GFS (end-to-end ocean and air freight forwarding with value-added logistics).
- FY26 revenue of INR 11,003 Cr is split 75% ISCS / 25% GFS per the deck's own pie label.
- Serves "over 7,100 active customers, including 100 Fortune Global 500 companies"; the Fortune 500 customer count is charted rising 61 (FY22), 72 (FY23), 78 (FY24), 91 (FY25), 100 (FY26).
- FY26 revenue by customer industry is stated in the deck's own prose as "Industrials (32%), Automotive (25%), Consumer (14%) and Tech & Tech Infra (12%)"; the accompanying pie also carries Rail and Utilities 7.5%, Healthcare 1.5% and two residual values (2.4%, 4.6%) against a single "Others" label, so the smallest slices are not reliably bound and are not asserted.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Freight market context] The deck charts the World Container Index ($ per 40ft container) from Mar-22 to Mar-26 with plotted values of 8200, 5800, 1791, 1404, 2929, 4775, 2368, 1761 and 2279; the point-to-date binding is not reliably preserved in extraction, so individual dates are not assigned.
- [Governance] Board chaired by Executive Chairman R. Dinesh with Vikas Chadha as Managing Director and five Independent Directors (B Sriram, Gauri Kumar, Tarun Khanna, K Ananth Krishnan, Narayan K Seshadri); global leadership includes R Vaidhyanathan (Global CFO) and regional CEOs for India/MEA, APAC & GFS, and Europe & North America.
- [Reporting definitions] The deck's headline metrics are adjusted: Adj EBITDA excludes ESOPs, forex gain/loss and redundancy costs; Adj PBT excludes exceptional items, redundancy cost and the TVS ILP InvIT gain; Operational PAT removes InvIT gains and exceptional items. Reported and adjusted figures diverge materially (e.g. FY26 EBITDA 782.6 vs Adjusted EBITDA 773.1; FY26 PBT 168.5 vs Adjusted PBT 99.3), so the label on each figure matters.
- [Disclosure status] The presentation is marked "STRICTLY PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL" / "CONFIDENTIAL" on several pages despite being filed with BSE and NSE under Regulation 30.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: TVS Supply Chain Solutions is an India-based multinational that pioneered the supply chain solutions market in India, evolving from automotive logistics into a diversified, global, asset-light and tech-led provider. It designs, orchestrates and optimises supply chains across the entire value chain from sourcing to consumption for leading customers across industrial, technology, consumer and other high-growth sectors. Operations are organised into two segments: Integrated Supply Chain Solutions (ISCS) and Global Forwarding Solutions (GFS).
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Integrated Supply Chain Solutions (ISCS):** Sourcing and procurement, Integrated transportation, Logistics operation centres, In-plant logistics operations, Finished warehousing, Aftermarket fulfilment, Supply chain consulting, Closed loop logistics, Spares logistics, Break-fix, refurbishment & engineering support, Courier and consignment management, Integrated Facility Management (IFM)
- **Global Forwarding Solutions (GFS):** End-to-end freight forwarding across ocean, air and land, Distribution, Warehousing and at-port storage, Value-added services

latest_quarter.body: ISCS margins improved via Europe recovery and operating leverage; GFS margins structurally lower but improved via cost optimization offsetting rate pressure; Employee costs up due to inflation/new projects but offset by 'Project One' cost takeouts; IndAS 116 costs rose slightly due to new North America site go-live.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: Double-digit to early teen growth expected for FY27. Margin: ISCS target 9.5%-10%; GFS cautious due to rate volatility; Consolidated Adj EBITDA margin trajectory towards 7.3%-7.4% initially, medium-term aspiration 10.5%-11% (ISCS) and 6%-6.5% (GFS). Order Inflow: Targeting 12%-15% of prior year revenue as new wins (achieved 12.1% in FY26). Capex: Asset-light model; no significant fixed asset investment; focus on working capital and tech integration.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs 6,100 cr total pipeline; Q4 new wins Rs 523.7 cr (record high, 21% of Q4 FY25 revenue); Typical conversion ratio ~22%; Wins span EV, electrical equipment, home appliances, retail, IT services, and industrial automation.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Acquisition of Swamy & Sons 3PL (completed May 2026) for FMCG/consumption depth in India; MOU with ALA for Defense/Aerospace entry (high certification barriers); 'China Plus One' relocation trends benefiting India manufacturing clients; Cross-sell/upsell within 100 Fortune 500 clients (added 9 new in FY26).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- The Company has a formal Dividend Distribution Policy setting out internal and external factors the Board weighs in determining pay-out. For FY26 the Directors decided not to recommend any dividend, choosing to conserve resources for future growth; no amount was transferred to reserves and no public deposits were accepted. Overall stance is reinvestment-led, prioritising internal capital for growth over distributions.
- Persistent gender-diversity gap: women comprise only ~8% of total employees and workers, 20% of the Board of Directors, and 0% of Key Managerial Personnel.
- High permanent-employee attrition: FY26 turnover rate for permanent employees was ~31% (33% female, 31% male), broadly in line with prior years.
- Community and environmental initiatives under 'TVS SCS Cares': restored six village ponds improving safe water access for 5,000+ residents, planted 5,000 palm-tree saplings for green cover/biodiversity, ran a village medical camp serving 150+ villagers, and collected 108.71 kg of waste in a coastal clean-up drive.
- Global CSR/volunteering programmes across geographies (Melbourne food-donation drive, North America hygiene/shelter donations, TVS SCS Europe 'Save the Children' fundraiser).
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone only, with no external assurance obtained for the reporting period — a limitation on the scope and independent verification of sustainability disclosures.
- Sustainability approach positioned as anchored in transparency, accountability and continuous improvement, with a Remuneration and Diversity policy in place.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TVS Supply Chain Solutions describes itself as a tech-led and asset-light supply chain solutions provider, so the FY26 report's routed sections disclose no plant/capacity capex projects with rupee outlays or commissioning timelines; expansion is organic and contract-led rather than fixed-asset-led. During FY26 the company re-organised its segment structure, unifying the erstwhile ISCS and Integrated Facility Management (IFM) capabilities into a single ISCS segment to deliver bundled, end-to-end services tailored to client needs, while Global Forwarding Solution (GFS) continues to house freight forwarding. Geographic and customer expansion came through strategic contract wins: a significant India contract with a leading global wind-turbine manufacturer, a European win with a leading multinational retail chain, and encircling/growth of North America operations with a leading global agricultural-equipment manufacturer. New business development added ~INR 1,206.74 crores of additional revenue in FY26, and the number of Fortune 500 customers serviced grew to 100 (from 91 in FY25). No forward financial guidance, buyback, or dividend policy statement appears in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

deepdive.thesis: TVS SCS delivered a spectacular FY26 finish with Q4 revenue crossing Rs 3,000 cr (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 80 bps to 7.3%, driven by a record Rs 524 cr in new business wins and a structural turnaround in Europe. The acquisition of Swamy & Sons and robust Rs 6,100 cr order pipeline position the company for sustained double-digit growth in FY27, shifting the narrative from recovery to accelerated expansion.

open.item: Company remains confident of delivering its target of double-digit revenue growth even in geographies with lower growth rates.
Increasing focus on specialised, higher-margin services and solutions to strengthen the quality of earnings and support sustainable margin improvement.
Partnership with Italy-based ALA Group to initially serve the India market and build a differentiated position in the Aerospace and Defence supply chain sector.
Accelerating adoption of Artificial Intelligence, including emerging Agentic AI, to automate processes, improve decision-making and enhance productivity across operations.
Driving operational efficiency through continuous improvement, process simplification and disciplined cost management to scale profitably.
Strengthening strategic carrier partnerships and capacity procurement capabilities across selected lanes to maintain service reliability in Global Forwarding Solutions.

Scheme of Amalgamation to merge wholly owned subsidiaries (TVS SCS Global Freight Solutions, White Data Systems, SPC International (India), FLEXOL Packaging (India) and Mahogany Logistics Services) into TVS Supply Chain Solutions Limited, pending NCLT sanction.
Management is pursuing strategic cost optimisation initiatives to enhance operating leverage.
